extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Department of Education funds (K-12 schools, institutions of higher education, school districts) and their legal/compliance/Title IX officers
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX notice and grievance rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for adopting, publishing, and notifying stakeholders of a recipient's Title IX non-discrimination policy and for adopting and publishing prompt and equitable grievance procedures (including the §106.45 process for formal complaints of sexual harassment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to persons and organizations (§106.8(a)/(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify an appropriately broad list of persons and organizations of the recipient's non-discrimination policy (moved into §106.8(a) as persons entitled to notification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department expects recipients to take effective steps to notify the listed persons and organizations so the educational community understands the policy and knows how to report sex discrimination. The final regulations do not prescribe a single mandatory form or method of notice (recognizing prior 1975 'initial' notice methods), but website posting alone does not satisfy this separate notification requirement. Examples of persons to notify include applicants for admission and employment, students, parents or legal guardians of elementary and secondary school students, employees, and unions or similar professional organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent posting on website and inclusion in handbooks/catalogs (§106.8(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must publish the non-discrimination policy and the Title IX Coordinator's contact information prominently on the recipient's website and include it in handbooks and catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department streamlined the list of publication types to reflect common institutional practices; website posting plus handbooks and catalogs is considered broad enough to ensure awareness. 'Prominent' is not rigidly defined by the rule, and recipients may place the policy on multiple pages (e.g., HR and admissions), provide a single accessible PDF, or post in multiple languages consistent with federal translation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Title IX Coordinator contact information in notices and postings
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-discrimination policy must include the Title IX Coordinator's contact information (including email) and that information must be published on the recipient's website if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differs from the Department's 2010 sample notice (which did not require a Title IX Coordinator or an email); the final rule requires these details so any person may report sex discrimination, including sexual harassment. The website posting requirement was revised to explicitly require the Coordinator's contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined list of publication types required to contain the policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule removes certain items from the prior regulatory list (e.g., announcements, bulletins, application forms) and retains/added items such as handbooks and catalogs, plus website posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department views some prior items as superfluous (e.g., application forms are unnecessary where applicants already receive notification). The streamlined list combined with website posting is intended to ensure relevant individuals see the policy without imposing unnecessary burdens on recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification obligation not satisfied by website posting alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting the policy on the recipient's website (required) does not fulfill the separate obligation to 'notify' the persons listed in §106.8(a); recipients must notify by some effective method separate and apart from website posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule intentionally does not prescribe the exact method of 'notification' (to allow flexibility and recognize historic 'initial' notice methods), but recipients must implement an effective separate notice practice for applicants, students, parents/guardians, employees, unions, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify unions and professional organizations holding agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify 'all unions or professional organizations holding collective bargaining agreements or professional agreements with the recipient' of the non-discrimination policy and Title IX Coordinator contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording is intended to capture unions and similar organizations at elementary/secondary and postsecondary levels; such organizations and their members need notice both for protection as employees and because they may have duties related to Title IX obligations. Posting on the website does not substitute for separate notification to these organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify parents and legal guardians of elementary and secondary students
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations restore and expand the list to explicitly require notice to 'parents or legal guardians of elementary and secondary school students.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added §106.6(g) to recognize parents' and guardians' legal rights to act on behalf of students under Title IX (including filing formal complaints). The change responds to concerns that excluding parents would risk underreporting and leave minors without effective advocacy or knowledge of reporting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications must not 'state' differential treatment on basis of sex (§106.8(b)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule prohibits recipients from using or distributing publications that 'state' the recipient treats applicants, students, or employees differently on the basis of sex except as permitted by Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department replaced prior language that prohibited publications that 'suggest[ ], by text or illustration' different treatment with the narrower 'state' formulation. The Department views requiring a non-discrimination policy, notification, and posting as sufficient and prefers evaluating explicit statements in publications; context is examinable and publications stating differential treatment remain actionable. Example enforcement contexts include a handbook describing a club as 'open to all boys.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Department will not routinely scrutinize graphics/illustrations for implied discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will not examine every graphic, photo, or illustration to determine whether it 'suggests' different treatment on the basis of sex and will not impose a requirement of proportional illustrative depictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a brochure for a nursing program showing mostly female students or a website photo need not be treated as evidence of discrimination absent explicit statements or context showing differential treatment. The Department considers scrutinizing all non-textual materials unreasonable and unlikely to yield fair assessments of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures must be prompt and equitable; sexual-harassment formal complaints must follow §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt and publish 'prompt and equitable' grievance procedures for complaints of sex discrimination generally, and must have a grievance process that complies with §106.45 for formal complaints of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule clarifies that formal complaints of sexual harassment are subject to the §106.45 process. While actual knowledge can arise via third-party reporting, the 'formal complaint' definition precludes third parties from filing a formal complaint; a formal complaint must be filed by a complainant or signed by the Title IX Coordinator. The Department revised §106.8(c) to make these points explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may disclose applicable Title IX exemptions and must reflect applicability in policy language
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-discrimination policy must accurately reflect whether Title IX (or subparts) applies to the recipient or particular programs and the final regulations use the phrase 'permitted by title IX or this part' to encompass statutory and regulatory exemptions (including religious exemptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients with exemptions are not making false representations by complying with §106.8 provided the policy includes qualifiers such as 'unless subpart C of this part does not apply.' The Department permits recipients to state on websites/publications any statutory/regulatory exemptions that apply to them; inquiries about applicability may be referred to the Title IX Coordinator or the Assistant Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department retains ability to address sex stereotyping and implicit discrimination in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the rule uses 'state' rather than 'suggest' language, the Department asserts this does not change its ability to evaluate publications for statements of different treatment based on sex, including under theories of sex stereotyping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department distinguishes between 'stating' differential treatment and 'suggesting' it by illustration; it will consider context and may reach similar enforcement results where a publication's text constitutes a statement of different treatment. Commenters' concerns about narrowing judicially recognized sex-stereotyping theories are acknowledged but the Department maintains enforcement tools remain adequate.
